note: Literature confirms high frequencies of dystonia (94%), corpus callosum abnormalities (70%), and anterior commissure hypoplasia/agenesis (66%) in ACBD6 deficiency, supporting their utility as key discriminators.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 45 individuals with bi-allelic ACBD6 variants, dystonia was observed in 94%, alongside characteristic midline malformations including corpus callosum abnormalities in 70% and hypoplasia/agenesis of the anterior commissure in 66%.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: The most conspicuous and common movement disorder was dystonia (94%), frequently leading to early-onset progressive postural deformities (97%) ... Midline brain malformations including corpus callosum abnormalities (70%), hypoplasia/agenesis of the anterior commissure (66%), short midbrain and small inferior cerebellar vermis (38% each) as well as hypertrophy of the clava (24%) were common neuroimaging findings.

evidence.text: Review of genetic movement disorders notes that ACBD6 mutations present with progression into dystonia and parkinsonism alongside hypoplasia or agenesis of the anterior commissure.
